line: The home game where everybody sees every flop is the same home game where everybody swears pocket aces are cursed.
why: One sentence puts two things every home-game regular has seen side by side and leaves the viewer to ask why they go together.

line: "My aces always get cracked." Next time you say it, finish the sentence: against how many players?
why: It opens on the exact sentence the viewer has said out loud and hands it back unfinished.

line: Nobody at your table ever folds, and you still wonder why your pocket aces keep losing.
why: It names the viewer's own table and their own complaint in one breath, with a dry edge that makes the answer feel obvious and still unseen.

line: Your pocket aces don't always get cracked. You just keep letting five people try.
why: It contradicts the belief in six words and turns the blame on something the viewer does every session.

line: Before you call the app rigged because your aces lost again, count how many players stayed in the hand.
why: Anyone who has muttered 'rigged' at an app is caught mid-thought and given something to check instead.
